items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: During the tour we were engaged to play a big ball in St. Moritz, Switzerland, for the millionaire shipping magnate Niarkos

ctx.x: The tour started the 8th of February. There were three booking agents handling this tour, two Italians and one Italo-American. One travelled with us. We were travelling by train. His name was Robert Burnier and we gave him the name of the "Creep" because he was tall, skinny, wore a black overcoat and hat and seemed to be always creeping around a corner like Mack the Knife.

During the tour we were engaged to play a big ball in St. Moritz, Switzerland, for the millionaire shipping magnate Niarkos, who was the brother in law of Onassis, another shipping magnate. The ball was given in the Palace Hotel which is the largest and most expensive hotel in that resort. And we also had rooms in that hotel.

We were on the bandstand which was about 15 inches high and I was standing at the left of the bandstand when one of the male guests came by on crutches. Just when he arrived at my side, one of the crutches slipped and I had the reflex just in time to catch him and prevent him from falling. I was sorry for this after, because the son of a bitch didn't thank me or even look at me. I regretted I had not let him fall and break his goddamn neck.
